title: Inquest in OPP arrest; Man died at cop station
article: More than three years after a man died of a gunshot wound inside the Port Credit OPP detachment, an inquest is set to start this January.
James Maltar, 45, died Sept. 18, 2005, while under arrest. Inquests are mandatory whenever a person dies in custody.

The inquest will examine all circumstances around Maltar's death; OPP policies and procedures for transporting and booking a person; and use-of-force training for officers. The jury can make recommendations to prevent other deaths under similar circumstances.
The three-week inquest begins in Toronto Jan. 17 and will hear evidence from at least 20 witnesses.
A Special Investigations Unit report released in August 2006 cleared an OPP officer of any criminal wrongdoing, concluding Maltar shot himself with a police gun.
The SIU's handling of the case was criticized by Ontario's ombudsman.
Slightly wounded while struggling with two officers inside the detachment, Maltar used an officer's gun to shoot himself in the head, an SIU statement said.
Maltar was taken to the OPP detachment in handcuffs after a traffic stop on Hwy. 403 in Mississauga where he failed to identify himself.
Once inside, SIU investigators concluded, Maltar was going to be re-handcuffed after being processed on several charges.
He appeared to comply with the order, "then started wrestling with the officer."

A female officer pulled on Maltar's arm as he tried to leave the station, the SIU said. Investigators said Maltar "was bigger and stronger than both officers and it appears that his level of agitation gave him even more strength. Pepper spray and baton blows by the female officer were ineffective."

The SIU said he grabbed the female officer's pistol. She then fired twice, one slug driving through Maltar's wrist and out his palm, the second bullet grazing his upper arm. "About the same time, Mr. Maltar shot himself in the head" with the officer's pistol, the SIU said.

Maltar's brother Rob said: "When all the evidence points one way and the SIU says, 'Oh, no, we're going the other way,' it just doesn't make sense and that's why we appealed to the ombudsman to take this on."
Maltar's family is suing the OPP.
